 Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1.

Mr. B.D. Jha, learned counsel for the applicants through V.C.
2.

The instant petition has been preferred under Section 528 of B.N.S.S. wherein the present applicants are challenging the proceedings of Criminal Case No. 2287 of 2024, State vs. Saurabh Thapa & others, wherein the present applicants are facing trial for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504, 498A IPC read with Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act pending in the court VIth Addl. Civil Judge(Sr. Div.)/ACJM, Dehradun.
3.

entities.text: VIth Addl. Civil Judge(Sr. Div.)/ACJM, Dehradun
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that applicant no. 1 married with the respondent no. 2/complainant on 15.11.2021,however due to some differences, respondent no. 2/ complainant left her matrimonial house and since then she is living separately.

4. The allegations appear to be matrimonial in nature, and so far as offence punishable under Section 354 IPC is concerned, after investigation same was struck of, since no evidence was found in respect of the said offence.
In para 6 of the affidavit it is submitted that applicant no. 1 tried his best to save the matrimonial life and wants to live with respondent no. 2.
If this is so, then the efforts may be made for amicable settlement.
5. Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State accepts notice for respondent no. 1.
6. Issue notice to respondent no. 2 returnable within three weeks.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant shall take steps to serve respondent no. 2 within a week.

8. List this case on 07.08.2024.
